title: A timestamp a client sends carries its UTC offset
intent: A date and time without a UTC offset names no instant: ten in the morning is a different moment in every zone. Stored as if it were UTC, it puts a writer in any other zone off by that zone's offset, and nothing reports it. The published API contract already asks for the offset, since a date-time there is the RFC 3339 form, whose offset is required. So timestamp text without one is refused wherever a request schema reads it, and a declared filter refuses a bound without one; the refusal names the fix. Reading a value without an offset as UTC, for a sender known to send UTC without saying so, is the framework's one way around it, and it is an escape a person decides and a reviewer sees.
reference: The rule fails closed by name. Every reference to NaiveMeansUtc is refused: as a name, as an attribute (core.NaiveMeansUtc, terp.core.NaiveMeansUtc), through getattr with that literal name, in a quoted annotation, and under every name the file binds to it by an import alias, an assignment or a type alias, at each use. So is a class or a re-export of that name from anywhere, and an import of terp.core.timestamps, the boundary's own machinery. A Literal value is text, not the escape. A plain datetime field needs nothing, and neither does a datetime query parameter forwarded to a declared filter: at run time BaseSchema refuses timestamp text without an offset wherever Pydantic reads a datetime, as a 422 at its place, and the filter refuses a bound without one as a 400 that names it (ADR 0206). The rule holds every root that ships Python, a worker as much as the app; terp.core, which defines the boundary and its escape, is neither's user.

runtime.rationale: The schema holds the invariant itself. BaseSchema puts the refusal in front of every datetime Pydantic validates for it, in a field, a list, a mapping, a union or a nested model, under the name Pydantic reads it by, so timestamp text without a UTC offset is a 422 at its place; a declared filter refuses a bound without one as a 400 that names the filter. A subclass that replaces the schema hook is refused when it is defined. The build-time half governs the framework's one way around the refusal, so taking it is never quiet.
